To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the molecular ordering of polylactides during the wet spinning method depends on the molar masses and d-lactid content of the polymer and that the molecular ordering affects the mechanical properties of PLA fibres.
PLA fibres with lower content of d-lactic acid isomers are characterized by higher tendency for crystallization and higher possibility to undergo α' to α phase transition.
the molecular structure of PLA has a significant impact on the molecular ordering and phase transition of the wet-spun fibres.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of obtaining fibres of different crystalline forms and mechanical properties by using different molecular structures of PLA.
the influence of the molar mass of PLA and its isomerisation degree (d-lactide content) on the molecular ordering and the crystalline forms (α’ and alpha form) of the obtained fibers.
the influence of molecular structure (molar mass and d-isomer content) of PLA on the molecular ordering and the α’–α transition during the wet spinning method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molar mass of PLA is the key factor influencing the molecular ordering and crystalline structure of PLA fibres, whereas the content of d-lactic isomer is of secondary importance.
the molecular structure of PLA has a significant impact on the crystalline forms (α’ and a), the molecular ordering and the physical properties of the obtained wet spinning fibres.
the PLA fibres with higher molecular ordering and the α form were characterised by higher mechanical properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wet spinning method can be used to manufacture PLA fibres with different properties, depending on the molar weight and content of d- and l-lactide.
the wet spinning process can be used to produce fibres with different crystalline structures and mechanical properties.

PLA with a lower molar mass and lower content of d-lactalde is more prone to crystallisation and the formation of the α form, which is reflected in the higher values of the Young’s modulus and tensile strength of the fibres.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molar mass of PLA and the content of d-lactic acid in its structure are crucial for the formation of the crystalline structure of fibres and for their mechanical properties.
the molar mass of PLA and its content of the d-lactide monomer have a significant effect on the crystalline forms of fibres and their physical properties.
the molecular structure of PLA influences its crystallisation during the wet spinning of PLA fibres.
